meta.title: Analyze
meta.description: Analyze one Deadlock hero in depth: win and pick rate trends, standing among its peers, builds and matchups, with sample sizes on every number.

title: Analyze
description: Pick a hero and a scope. Every number below uses the same data and rules as the Meta and hero pages, with its sample size alongside.
unknownHeroDescription: That hero isn’t in the current hero list. Pick one above.

roles.title: Choose a hero to analyze
roles.description: Pick a hero above to see its trends, standing among its peers, builds and matchups. Meanwhile, here is how each role performs in this scope.
roles.clear: The top role’s 95% interval sits entirely above every other role’s.
roles.overlap: The roles’ 95% intervals overlap, so no role is clearly ahead of the others in this scope.
roles.source: Roles come from the game’s hero list.
roles.none: No role data in this scope.

summary.noMatches: No matches for {hero} in this scope, so there is nothing to measure. Try a longer window or a broader rank band.
summary.lowSample: Low sample: {matches} matches (under {threshold}). The numbers below are shown for reference only: they aren’t ranked, compared or used for insights. Try a longer window or a broader rank band.
summary.winWhy: Won {wins} of {matches} matches. The 95% interval is {low}–{high}.
summary.winWhyNoTrend: Won {wins} of {matches} matches. The 95% interval is {low}–{high}. The weekly trend needs a non-Low sample in both weeks, so none is shown.
summary.pickWhy: Share of matches with {hero} in this scope: hero matches ÷ (all hero matches ÷ 12). {rank, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}} most picked of {count} heroes.

trends.title: Win rate and pick rate trends
trends.range: Daily values for the selected window, {window}: {dates} ({days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}), {rank}. Patch days are marked.
trends.missing: The source has no daily data for {missing} of these days, so the charts show {shown}.
trends.winRateDescription: Daily, with the 50% line for reference.

compare.title: Compared with other heroes
compare.description: Same window and rank band. Only heroes with enough data are ranked; Low-sample heroes are listed last, muted.
compare.lowSample: {hero} has a Low sample in this scope, so it isn’t ranked or compared.
compare.standing: {win, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}} highest win rate and {pick, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}} highest pick rate of {count} {group} with enough data.
compare.higher: Higher than the other {group} combined ({rate}, {delta}); the 95% intervals don’t overlap.
compare.lower: Lower than the other {group} combined ({rate}, {delta}); the 95% intervals don’t overlap.
compare.within: Not clearly different from the other {group} combined ({rate}): the intervals overlap or the gap is under 1 point.

builds.title: Build performance
builds.description: This week’s most-favorited community builds, those with tracked results first (a build counts when it was selected at game start).
builds.none: No community builds found for this hero.
builds.noTracked: None of this week’s most-favorited builds has tracked matches in this scope, so there is no build performance to show here. A longer window often has some; the <link>Builds page</link> uses the last 30 days for the same rank band.

matchups.title: Matchup analysis
matchups.description: Lane opponents with 100+ games, ranked by the edge of the 95% interval so small samples can’t top the list.

method.title: How to read this
method.sourceText: Public match data from deadlock-api.com, normal mode. Every number uses the window and rank band selected above (match average rank), the same numbers as the Meta and hero pages.
method.sampleText: Under {moderate} matches is a Low sample: shown muted, never ranked, compared or turned into an insight. Over {high} is High.
method.intervalsText: Win rates come with a 95% Wilson interval. A difference is called out only when two intervals don’t overlap and the gap is at least 1 percentage point.
method.limitsText: These are measured results, not causes. A higher win rate in a split doesn’t say why, and item win rates partly reflect who is already ahead.
